nodes.description: Hereditary coproporphyria is the block at coproporphyrinogen-III oxidase, late in the pathway. Because the lesion is downstream of the porphyrinogens, the subtype is separated from its acute siblings by quantifying porphyrins in urine and faeces rather than by the acute-attack chemistry they share. The block is also late enough that the disease is not purely neurovisceral: the GeneReviews chapter reports photosensitivity with bullae and skin fragility in about 20% of those who have had an acute attack.

nodes.description: Inherited porphyrias arise when pathogenic variants reduce activity of heme-biosynthesis enzymes or alter ALAS2 regulation, creating subtype-specific bottlenecks in porphyrin metabolism. Which step is blocked determines which intermediate accumulates and therefore which subtype a patient has, so each enzyme has its own node above -- the hydroxymethylbilane synthase, ALA dehydratase, coproporphyrinogen oxidase, protoporphyrinogen oxidase and uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase blocks -- alongside the erythroid UROS and FECH/ALAS2 nodes below.
